description: Frozen PROCEDURE and evidence schema for the tier track-record ledger (tier-enforcement-implementation slice 3, steps tier-s3a-ledger-schema-and-perimeter and tier-s3b-promotion-demotion-emitters; convene 20260611T130035Z conditions 7 + 10). The procedure, evidence schema, and reviewer-distinctness invariant are FROZEN now; the N/M/window threshold VALUES are provisional and operator-ratified after a calibration window — never permanent law before data exists.

ledger.governed_perimeter: The ledger directory and _dev/state/session-tier/** sit INSIDE the mutation-plan-gate governed-path perimeter (process-tier-rule.yaml add_registry.adds.mutation-plan-gate.paths; convene condition 7). The writer verifies this at write time and records governed_perimeter_verified in the ledger header.

file_shape.model_id: producer model id as recorded in durable artifacts
file_shape.governed_perimeter_verified: boolean — canonical rule perimeter covered the ledger path at last write
file_shape.entries: array of entry objects (shape below), append-only

entry_shape.entry_id: deterministic id: sha1 over plan_artifact + distinct_review.artifact + distinct_review.at + work_unit (idempotent appends)
entry_shape.task_id: plan/task id the coordinated run executed
entry_shape.plan_artifact: repo-relative path to the task plan JSON (must exist on disk at derivation time)
entry_shape.scope_class: one of scope_classes below, derived mechanically from the plan

producer.actor_id: producing coordinator actor id from durable artifacts (session-tier stamp model > task-outcome produced_by_actor_id > plan produced_by_actor_id)
producer.model: producer model string when a session-tier stamp is available, else null
producer.session_id: producing session id when known, else null
producer.stamp_artifact: repo-relative path to the session-tier stamp used, else null

entry_shape.changed_files: declared coverage from the plan (bounded_plan.steps[].files_touched + scope_identity.owned_artifacts)
entry_shape.evidence_refs: repo-relative paths of every durable artifact the entry was derived from

distinct_review.artifact: distinct_reviews[].artifact — must exist on disk for a grade-bearing entry

entry_shape.work_unit: slice/step id(s) or commit hash being graded — required for grade-bearing entries (schema 1.1 additive)
entry_shape.review_artifact: repo-relative path to the review artifact that covers this work unit — required for grade-bearing entries (schema 1.1 additive)
entry_shape.review_at: ISO timestamp of the review that covers this work unit — must be AFTER work_unit_completed_at for a grade-bearing entry (schema 1.1 additive)
entry_shape.work_unit_completed_at: ISO timestamp of when the work unit (slice/step/commit) was completed — derived from derived_at of the entry or the output artifact; stale-pre-execution rejection compares review_at against this (schema 1.1 additive)
entry_shape.binding_basis: how coverage was established: 'artifact-path-match' | 'artifact-content-match' | 'work-unit-declared' | 'no-binding' — GRADE-BEARING WHITELIST (W3): only 'artifact-path-match' and 'artifact-content-match' may produce a grade-bearing entry; 'work-unit-declared' is recordable but is NEVER grade-bearing (yields ungraded + rejection_reason 'binding-too-weak-declared-only'); 'no-binding' triggers stale-pre-execution or no-work-unit-binding rejection (schema 1.1 additive; W3 categorical whitelist 20260611T)
entry_shape.rejection_reason: present only when a grade-bearing entry was downgraded to ungraded by the binding enforcement: 'stale-pre-execution-review' | 'no-work-unit-binding' | 'binding-too-weak-declared-only' | null (schema 1.1 additive; W3 adds 'binding-too-weak-declared-only')
entry_shape.grade: clean | failed | ungraded — derived ONLY from the distinct reviewer's durable verdict via verdict_classification; the appender exposes no input that sets a grade
entry_shape.grade_basis: verdict-classification | reviewer-identity-unresolved | no-distinct-review | stale-pre-execution-review | no-work-unit-binding | binding-too-weak-declared-only
entry_shape.graded_by: reviewer_actor for grade-bearing entries; null for ungraded
entry_shape.source_artifacts: every file read to derive the entry
entry_shape.derived_by: invoking actor id (informational only — never a grade source)

scope_classes.derivation: mechanical, from the plan: client_code set -> client-delivery; else any coverage entry under instructions/canonical/**, tools/kernel/**, or .claude/** -> system-kernel; else any coverage entry under frameworks/** -> framework; else system-other

verdict_classification.description: Grades pass through from the distinct reviewer's recorded verdict; they never originate in the appender. Verdicts are classified against these enumerated lists after lowercasing/trimming; anything unlisted is ungraded — no fuzzy matching, no grade laundering.

reviewer_distinctness_invariant.description: Producer-can't-self-validate, enforced mechanically in the writer (convene condition 7): a grade-bearing entry is written only when the reviewing actor is DISTINCT INTELLIGENCE from the producing actor. Same-model actors are parallel contexts, not distinct intelligence (dispatch-routing-rule), so distinctness is checked at model-family granularity.
reviewer_distinctness_invariant.mechanism: actorSignature() extracts a model-family token (fable | opus | sonnet | haiku | gpt | gemini | claude | operator) from each actor string; the write is REJECTED when the families match, when either family is unresolvable, or when the normalized actor strings are equal. Fail-closed: an unresolvable reviewer identity can never produce a grade.
reviewer_distinctness_invariant.write_rule: Grade-bearing entries (clean | failed) are written only by deriving from a distinct reviewer's durable artifacts (plan-task-review-state distinct_reviews + the review artifact on disk) or by an out-of-band higher-tier process editing under operator authority. The producing coordinator never writes its own grade.

work_unit_binding_invariant.description: Schema 1.1 additive invariant (W2 remediation, amendment 20260611T152855Z; W3 categorical whitelist 20260611T). Reviewer identity is necessary but insufficient for a grade-bearing entry: the review must demonstrably cover the graded work unit. A grade-bearing entry REQUIRES a distinct review whose artifact demonstrably covers the work unit (mechanical check: review artifact path contains a work_unit token, or the review artifact's on-disk content references a commit/slice/evidence file declared as the work unit). Reviews timestamped before the work unit's completion are REJECTED as stale-pre-execution — the entry is written as ungraded with rejection_reason 'stale-pre-execution-review', never silently graded. Fail-closed: no binding established → entry written as ungraded with rejection_reason 'no-work-unit-binding'.
work_unit_binding_invariant.grade_bearing_basis_whitelist: CATEGORICAL (W3): only binding_basis ∈ { 'artifact-path-match', 'artifact-content-match' } may produce a grade-bearing (clean|failed) entry. 'work-unit-declared' is a recordable basis value (the review post-dates completion and a work_unit was declared) but it is NEVER grade-bearing — such entries are written ungraded with rejection_reason 'binding-too-weak-declared-only'. Staleness and binding are separate gates; passing timestamp order does not prove review scope.
work_unit_binding_invariant.mechanism: deriveWorkUnitBinding(review, workUnit, workUnitCompletedAt) in the writer: (1) no workUnit declared → binding_basis='no-binding', rejection_reason='no-work-unit-binding' (checked first, unconditional); (2) stale-pre-execution check — review.at < workUnitCompletedAt → binding_basis='no-binding', rejection_reason='stale-pre-execution-review'; (3) path-match check — review.artifact path contains a workUnit token → binding_basis='artifact-path-match'; (4) content-match check — review artifact on-disk content contains a workUnit token → binding_basis='artifact-content-match'; (5) workUnit declared, review post-dates completedAt, path/content checks fail → binding_basis='work-unit-declared', rejection_reason='binding-too-weak-declared-only' (NEVER grade-bearing, W3 categorical).
work_unit_binding_invariant.write_rule: A grade-bearing entry is rejected (downgraded to ungraded + rejection_reason) when: (a) stale-pre-execution (review.at < work_unit_completed_at), (b) no-work-unit-binding (work_unit is absent and grade is clean|failed — caller must declare a work_unit for grade-bearing entries), or (c) binding-too-weak-declared-only (work_unit declared and review post-dates completion but review artifact path/content does not demonstrably cover the work unit — W3 categorical gate). Ungraded entries may omit work_unit and binding_basis.

procedure.promotion: When a model accumulates promotion_n CONSECUTIVE clean distinct-review outcomes within one scope_class, emit-candidacy.cjs emits a promotion candidacy artifact — an operator-gated PROPOSAL to relax specific adds for that model+scope_class. Ratification happens only by the operator editing instructions/canonical/process-tier-rule.yaml with provenance (operator_ratified + convene receipt). The witness is up-lineage: a tier is promoted by the tier above it plus the operator, never by itself.
procedure.demotion: When a model accumulates demotion_m FAILED distinct-review outcomes within window_days inside one scope_class, emit-candidacy.cjs emits a demotion candidacy artifact the same way. The failure classifier is owned by the distinct reviewer (verdict_classification over reviewer-recorded verdicts), never the producer.
procedure.candidacy_artifacts: _dev/reports/analysis/tier-track-record/candidacies/<type>__<model-key>__<scope-class>__<dedupe>.json (TierGraduationCandidacy/1.0) — inside the governed perimeter. Deduped by evidence set; re-runs never duplicate.
procedure.never_auto_applied: No ledger machinery ever mutates process-tier-rule.yaml or any canonical surface. Candidacies are Decision-shaped proposals: candidacy artifact + (optional, flag-gated) Dart 'Decision Needed' task assigned to the operator.

thresholds.note: PROVISIONAL starting values (convene condition 10 / G10) — recorded so promotion criteria are not retrofitted to flatter early results, but explicitly NOT law: operator ratifies final values after a calibration window of real ledger data. Changing them is an edit to this frozen schema file (itself inside the tools/kernel/** governed perimeter).
